skill.name: content-reviewer
skill.description: Use when you need to review influencer content before launch against a campaign brief, brand guidelines, FTC disclosure needs, platform specs, and C3 ART quality criteria. It returns an approve, revise, or reject decision with creator-ready feedback.
skill.summary: Reviews influencer content for brand fit, message accuracy, disclosure compliance, quality, and launch readiness.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: The audit found no prompt-injection attempt, executable command path, or malicious filesystem traversal in the reviewed Markdown files. Most static findings are false positives from fixed documentation links, inline code formatting, template fences, connector placeholders, or platform labels. One low-risk network issue remains: the standalone fallback can fetch mutable reference content from GitHub at runtime.

remediation.suggestion: Pin the raw GitHub fallback to a version tag or bundled reference file, and require user confirmation before fetching remote reference content.

content.value_statement: Influencer posts can miss brand, message, or disclosure requirements before launch. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured approval gate with evidence and creator-ready feedback.
actual_capabilities: Reviews draft posts, captions, links, or media notes against a campaign brief and brand guidelines.
Scores brand alignment, message accuracy, compliance, creative quality, and technical specifications.
Enforces C3 ART veto checks for FTC disclosure and claim integrity before approval.
Produces one launch decision: approved, approved with minor changes, revisions required, or rejected.
Creates constructive creator feedback and an auditor-style handoff with scoring fields.
limitations: Requires the user to provide the content submission, campaign brief, platform, and disclosure context.
Does not replace legal review for regulated claims or jurisdiction-specific advertising advice.
Cannot verify live platform metadata without user-provided evidence or configured connectors.
Does not draft campaign briefs or partnership contracts; it reviews content after criteria exist.

use_cases.title: Approve Creator Drafts
use_cases.description: Check a creator submission against the campaign brief before the post goes live.

use_cases.title: Screen Disclosure Risk
use_cases.description: Identify missing ad disclosures or unsubstantiated claims that require rejection or resubmission.

use_cases.title: Standardize Feedback
use_cases.description: Turn review findings into clear, constructive feedback that creators can act on quickly.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Draft
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single content submission.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this influencer content draft for launch readiness. Platform: [platform]. Campaign: [campaign]. Content: [paste caption, link, or media notes]. Brief: [paste key requirements]. Give one decision and creator feedback.

prompt_templates.title: Check Against Brief
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review with brand and message criteria.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare this creator submission against our campaign brief and brand guidelines. Identify pass or fail for brand alignment, message accuracy, compliance, quality, and technical specs. Then write feedback for the creator.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Claims And Disclosure
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this sponsored creator post for disclosure placement, claim substantiation, platform requirements, and prohibited claims. Treat missing disclosure or unsupported claims as reject-level issues. Explain the decision in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Run Full Launch Gate
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced end-to-end approval gate with handoff fields.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the full content-reviewer launch gate for this submission. Use the C3 ART content benchmark, produce scores, record any veto result, map the decision to the handoff status, and create creator-ready revision notes.

output_examples.input: A TikTok draft for a protein campaign includes strong visuals but no visible sponsored disclosure.
output_examples.output: Decision: rejected. The review explains that the missing disclosure is a reject-level compliance issue, then lists required resubmission fixes and positive creative notes.

output_examples.input: An Instagram Reel follows the brief but misses one required promo code in the caption.
output_examples.output: Decision: revisions required. The output separates must-fix messaging gaps from optional quality suggestions and provides a concise creator feedback message.

output_examples.input: A YouTube Short includes disclosure, required product claims, correct CTA, and platform-ready specs.
output_examples.output: Decision: approved. The review records pass evidence across brand, message, compliance, quality, and technical checks.

best_practices: Provide the brief, brand guidelines, platform, caption, media notes, and sponsorship status before review.
Separate must-fix compliance issues from optional creative suggestions in creator feedback.
Keep internal veto IDs in the audit artifact and explain decisions to users in plain language.
anti_patterns: Do not approve sponsored content when disclosure is missing or unclear.
Do not use this skill to create the campaign brief or legal contract from scratch.
Do not treat soft quality penalties as automatic rejection when compliance and claims pass.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews influencer content submissions against a brief, brand rules, disclosure needs, claims, quality, and platform specs.

faq.question: Can it approve content for launch?
faq.answer: It can recommend an approval decision, but your team remains responsible for final business and legal approval.

faq.question: Does it give legal advice?
faq.answer: No. It flags disclosure and claim issues for review, but it does not replace legal counsel.

faq.question: What inputs should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the content draft, campaign brief, required messages, brand guidelines, platform, content type, and sponsorship context.

faq.question: How does it handle missing disclosures?
faq.answer: For sponsored content, missing or inadequate disclosure is treated as a reject-level issue that requires resubmission.

faq.question: Can it write feedback for creators?
faq.answer: Yes. It turns review findings into direct, constructive feedback that creators can use for revisions.
